preamble: Long QT Syndrome  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  HRS/EHRA/APHRS 2013 Channelopathy Guidelines / AHA/ACC 2017 Ventricular Arrhythmia Guidelines / ESC 2022 Ventricular Arrhythmia Guidelines  |  SCD and Arrhythmia Risk Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is there a history of resuscitated cardiac arrest or documented ventricular fibrillation attributed to LQTS?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — aborted SCA confirmed; highest-risk LQTS subgroup; ICD implantation Class I regardless of QTc; recurrent SCA risk ~10%/year without ICD; immediate ICD implantation and beta-blocker required

questions.question: Is there documented torsades de pointes (TdP) or polymorphic VT on telemetry, Holter, or event monitor?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — confirmed TdP; direct mechanism of syncope and SCA in LQTS; establishes high-risk classification; ICD strongly recommended; left cardiac sympathetic denervation (LCSD) consideration

questions.question: Is QTc ≥500 ms on resting 12-lead ECG (Bazett correction, average of 3–5 beats)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — QTc ≥500 ms confirmed; >10-fold increased SCD risk vs. general population; independent high-risk marker per HRS/EHRA/APHRS; ICD consideration even in asymptomatic patients

questions.question: Is QTc 480–499 ms with accompanying syncope history, high-risk genotype (LQT2/LQT3), or family SCD history?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — moderately prolonged QTc with compounding risk features confirmed; cumulative risk exceeds isolated QTc threshold; ICD discussion warranted

questions.question: Is there T-wave alternans (beat-to-beat alternation in T-wave amplitude or polarity) or 2:1 AV block on ECG or Holter?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — T-wave alternans or 2:1 AV block confirmed; markers of severe repolarization instability; 2:1 AV block in neonatal LQTS (LQT3) carries very high mortality without pacing

questions.question: Is there confirmed Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome (biallelic KCNQ1 loss-of-function + congenital sensorineural deafness)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — JLN syndrome confirmed; most severe LQTS phenotype; near-universal arrhythmia events without treatment; ICD implantation in virtually all patients; LCSD adjunct strongly recommended

questions.question: Is the genotype LQT2 (KCNH2 pathogenic variant) or LQT3 (SCN5A gain-of-function), particularly with pore-region or dominant-negative mutations?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LQT2/LQT3 high-risk genotype confirmed; LQT2 pore mutations and LQT3 SCN5A variants carry higher arrhythmia rates than LQT1; genotype-specific therapy (mexiletine for LQT3) available

questions.question: Has the patient had ≥2 syncopal episodes on beta-blocker therapy, or syncope with a clearly identified LQTS trigger (swimming, auditory startle, sleep)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — recurrent or breakthrough syncope on therapy confirmed; beta-blocker failure; ICD implantation or LCSD escalation required; nadolol dose optimization before ICD if not yet maximized

questions.question: Is the patient regularly exposed to confirmed high-risk genotype-specific triggers without adequate precautions (competitive swimming for LQT1; alarm clocks / sudden noise for LQT2; bradycardia during sleep for LQT3)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — ongoing high-risk trigger exposure confirmed; immediate lifestyle modification counseling required; activity restrictions per genotype; QTc-prolonging drug avoidance (CredibleMeds review)

questions.question: Is there unexplained sudden cardiac death at age <40 years or unexplained drowning in a first- or second-degree relative?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — family SCD or drowning history confirmed; consistent with lethal LQTS event; raises risk classification; triggers cascade screening of all first-degree relatives

questions.question: Are there ≥2 first-degree relatives with confirmed LQTS or pathogenic variant in the same gene?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high-penetrance familial LQTS confirmed; indicates severe mutation with strong expressivity; higher likelihood of recurrent events across the family; genetic counseling required

questions.question: Is the patient currently taking one or more QTc-prolonging medications (antiemetics, antibiotics, antidepressants, antifungals) identified on CredibleMeds review?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — drug-induced QT prolongation risk confirmed; immediate medication reconciliation required; substitute non-QT-prolonging alternatives wherever possible; electrolyte correction (K⁺ ≥4.0, Mg²⁺ ≥0.85)

questions.question: Is there documented hypokalemia (K⁺ <3.5 mEq/L) or hypomagnesemia (Mg²⁺ <0.75 mmol/L) on labs?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — electrolyte depletion confirmed; potassium and magnesium are critical for cardiac repolarization; replaces electrolytes promptly; high-potassium diet and supplementation as needed
